title: Oakcrest Health - Private VPC Discovery
summary: Initial discovery for Oakcrest Health evaluating Redwood Private (VPC) - discussed VPC peering vs private endpoints, region/residency constraints, key management (KMS/HSM), audit logging, and SLA/uptime expectations. Agreed next steps: share architecture diagram, security pack, and propose pilot timeline + pricing.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-04-09 14:00 PT - Duration 49 mins - Attendees: Maya, Diego, Emily, Marcus, Priya
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone thanks for joining, this is Maya with Redwood, i'm the AE on this account, i'll let diego jump in for the deep network bits but just to set context Oakcrest is looking at Private deployment, right?
[00:14] Dr. Emily Rhodes: yep, thanks Maya. We want to run inference inside our AWS account, must be within us-east-1 for patient data residency. Interested in the private vpc option, curious about peering vs private endpoints and also the footprint - we have strict HIPAA controls.
[00:28] Diego Ramos: great, thanks. Quick question on topology - do you have existing Direct Connect or a transit gateway? or will this be over VPC peering?
[00:36] Marcus Lee: We already have a transit gateway and DX to our core datacenter. Ideally we want the Redwood nodes to live in our VPC and route through TGW. How do you handle routing and security groups?
[00:48] Diego Ramos: technically we support both models - private endpoints (AWS PrivateLink) and VPC peering. With PrivateLink you get an interface endpoint in your VPC and traffic never leaves the AWS network. With peering you have full L3 routing but you need route table entries and there's transitive peering limits; TGW often simplifies that. Our private deploy control plane can be customer-managed or we can host control plane but keep data plane in your VPC - lots of customers prefer customer-managed control plane for compliance.
[01:10] Priya Patel: when you say control plane, that means key material, logs etc - which parts live in our account? we need to know where KMS keys are, encryption at rest, audit logs.
[01:20] Maya Chen: good callout. For Private we offer two patterns: 1) fully customer-managed - the whole stack (control + data plane) runs in your VPC; 2) hybrid - control plane in Redwood-managed account with data plane in your VPC via PrivateLink. In hybrid, you can bring-your-own-KMS for disk encryption using customer-managed CMKs via cross-account roles.
[01:38] Dr. Emily Rhodes: any HSM support? our compliance wants HSM-backed keys for some workloads.
[01:44] Diego Ramos: yes, HSM support is possible. We integrate with AWS CloudHSM or external HSM via KMIP in the customer-managed model. There are some setup steps - network, IAM and policies - we'll share the reference guide.
[01:56] Marcus Lee: region restrictions - must stay in us-east-1, maybe also us-east-2 in future. Do you have availability zones requirements?
[02:04] Maya Chen: we can deploy to a single region you choose. For HA we recommend multi-AZ within the region. Dedicated capacity nodes can be pinned to AZs. If you want multi-region, we can talk replication and failover, but that increases complexity.
[02:18] Diego Ramos: also worth noting as AWS specifics - PrivateLink endpoints are regional; peering works cross-region only via inter-region peering (and there are limitations). If your compliance is strict on residency, keeping everything in us-east-1 and using PrivateLink into that VPC is usually simplest.
[02:36] Dr. Emily Rhodes: ok that helps. Performance - we're sensitive to latency for our triage models. How does latency look with traffic across PrivateLink vs peering?
[02:46] Diego Ramos: PrivateLink adds a tiny network hop but keeps traffic inside AWS edge, typically sub-ms to a few ms depending on AZ placement. Peering with colocated nodes in the same AZ will be slightly lower latency but operationally more complex. We also do batching and KV cache to reduce tokens/time.
[03:04] Marcus Lee: what's the onboarding timeline? we need to run a pilot with 2-3 models and run benchmarks against our latency SLO (p95 < 200ms).
[03:12] Maya Chen: typical pilot is 4-6 weeks: week 1-2 - infra and network setup, week 3 - run baseline benchmarks, week 4-6 - optimize batching/quantization with Diego and share cost/latency tradeoffs. We'll provide a pilot checklist.
[03:28] Priya Patel: audit logs and SIEM integration - can you forward audit events to our CloudWatch or Splunk?
[03:36] Diego Ramos: yes we can ship audit logs to your S3 bucket or CloudWatch Logs via cross-account role; we also support pushing to external SIEMs. For hybrid control plane we'll need to wire up cross-account IAM and a role that allows delivery of logs. There might be a small lag for log collection depending on retention settings.
[03:54] Dr. Emily Rhodes: Do you have SOC 2 or ISO certs? we have vendor assessment to fill out.
[04:00] Maya Chen: Redwood is SOC 2 Type II and we have ISO 27001 docs - i'll attach the security pack after the call and Diego will follow up on any technical questions.
[04:10] Marcus Lee: about network egress and cost - if we use your managed control plane does traffic egress to Redwood accounts and cause extra data transfer fees?
[04:18] Maya Chen: in hybrid mode data plane stays in your VPC so no egress for inference. In fully-hosted modes there could be inter-account transfer costs depending on topology. We'll call that out in the pricing/architecture doc.
[04:30] Diego Ramos: another detail: for model updates we do a canary workflow - we can push new model versions into a staging subset, smoke test, then route traffic; with private deployments you control rollout windows.
[04:42] Dr. Emily Rhodes: encryption in transit - do you support mTLS?
[04:46] Diego Ramos: yes, we support TLS and mutual TLS for service-to-service connections in the private deployment. We can also require client certs for endpoints.
[04:54] Maya Chen: just a quick question on stakeholders - who's going to own the pilot and procurement?
[04:58] Dr. Emily Rhodes: me for technical + Marcus for infra, procurement will be our vendor team - we'll loop them if we move forward.
[05:06] Marcus Lee: curious about IP/networking specifics - what's required in the VPC: a couple subnets, route tables, security groups, NACLs?
[05:14] Diego Ramos: minimal footprint is two private subnets across separate AZs for the serving nodes, an interface endpoint (if using PrivateLink) and IAM roles for cross-account access. We'll share a terraform snippet. Also inbound rules are pretty locked down - only your app subnets talk to the inference nodes.
[05:30] Priya Patel: cert rotation and key custody - how often do you rotate keys by default? and can we enforce rotation window?
[05:38] Maya Chen: we support customer rotation policies via KMS - you can set rotation every 30/90/365 days and we can integrate with your key rotation automation.
[05:46] Dr. Emily Rhodes: for the pilot we want a smoke test using our triage model, then measure p95 and token cost. Can you run a small benchmark in our VPC?
[05:56] Diego Ramos: absolutely, we'll need temporary test credentials and a small runway in your account; we'll run load tests and provide a benchmark spreadsheet. We'll also test batching and kv cache behavior.
[06:08] Maya Chen: pricing - we'll send both pilot pricing and a dedicated capacity outline. any budget constraints we should know?
[06:14] Marcus Lee: for the pilot we have a budgetary ceiling of $25k for the PoC. If numbers look reasonable we can expand.
[06:20] Maya Chen: got it, we'll craft a pilot proposal under that.
[06:24] Dr. Emily Rhodes: compliance questionnaire - i'll send over the vendor security questionnaire. can you fill it?
[06:30] Maya Chen: yes i'll do that and include the SOC2 pack.
[06:34] [09:34] Diego Ramos: (note: timestamp misaligns, speaker diarization sometimes off) technical note: if you want strict AZ locality we can pin nodes but there is tradeoff for resilience. For KV cache we store ephemeral state on local NVMe - encrypted. Persistent model artifacts are pulled from your S3 or a Redwood-managed repo depending on RW.
[07:02] Marcus Lee: what about dependency on specific instance types? we use latest Graviton and some metal - can you support ARM based instances / Graviton?
[07:10] Diego Ramos: currently our optimized kernels are on x86 GPUs (NVIDIA) for best throughput. Graviton CPU instances are okay for small models but for large LLMs we recommend NVIDIA GPUs; on-prem or dedicated options can be discussed for specialized hardware.
[07:24] Priya Patel: legal/procurement timeline - procurement needs 4 weeks for contracts after technical sign off. Just flagging.
[07:30] Maya Chen: thanks, that's helpful. We'll aim to align pilot timing with procurement.
[07:34] Dr. Emily Rhodes: any competitors you see in our space?
[07:38] Maya Chen: commonly mentioned are Anthropic (for hosted), OpenAI for API, and some customers build internal self-hosted stacks; i'll call those out in the follow up.
[07:48] Marcus Lee: ok next steps?
[07:50] Maya Chen: recap - Maya will share security pack, architecture doc (PrivateLink & TGW patterns), and pilot proposal + pricing; Diego will share helm/terraform snippets and a benchmark checklist; Emily/Marcus will send vendor questionnaire and grant demo creds/test IAM role. We'll schedule a follow up technical kickoff in 1 week.
[08:10] Dr. Emily Rhodes: sounds good, thanks everyone.
[08:14] Maya Chen: thanks all, we'll follow up with the docs.
[08:18] (call ends)
Notes: transcript includes several minor ASR errors and occasional speaker mislabels (Speaker 2 appears as Diego in some lines). References: security pack link (sent in chat): https://redwood.example.com/security/oakcrest, terraform snippet link: https://redwood.example.com/infra/oakcrest-terraform
